gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-fs-public-s: Authoritative and literary up top, Noto Serif Old Uyghur gives way to Public Sans below. Its stencil-cut letters carry mild bar variation, while the sans-serif body is hefty and broad, so a modest bump in heading size is all the separation needed.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-fs-supreme: Noto Serif Old Uyghur has a deep middle band and a subdued contrast across the alphabet. And Supreme, a sans with a thick, heavy strip of text, holds its letters open, so long paragraphs read crisply and without fuss.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-general-san: Literary weight leads in Noto Serif Old Uyghur, whose smooth, modest gradient in stroke sits above General Sans and its looped, tubing-like lines. One feels written, the other drawn.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-manrope: Slightly heavier verticals tug against lighter horizontals in Noto Serif Old Uyghur. Manrope below is a sans with no calligraphic modulation, and its bright open curves give the serif's literary voice a clear, friendly counterweight.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-montserrat: Understated stroke variation marks Noto Serif Old Uyghur, which carries a literary, authoritative tone across the page. And Montserrat, the sans-serif body, glides along in uninterrupted line width with oversized e and a counters, so a long passage moves smoothly.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-satoshi: Noto Serif Old Uyghur sits deep in the middle band, with mid-level stroke contrast and an authoritative, literary manner. Satoshi answers in a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and a plain, unshaded line that never swells.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-switzer: Switzer reads as a tall-waisted sans-serif of wire-like letterforms, with curves that never thin out at the turns. But Noto Serif Old Uyghur above it has arches that slim slightly leaving the stem, giving the page a literary, authoritative edge.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-work-sans: Letterpress-slug looks, modestly thick and thin, sit in Noto Serif Old Uyghur, while Work Sans below is a monoline skeleton with a high mean line. Different skeletons, one clear difference.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-archivo: Noto Serif Oriya has visible yet mild contrast and tall, bookish lowercase with compact extenders. But Archivo is the one with the commanding x-height, its sans curves opening outward instead of curling in.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-fs-asap: Noto Serif Oriya brings a quiet variation in line weight to each letter. Asap, a sans-serif with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, keeps a long passage readable and unhurried.
